newsitem.title: UK: Dollar gets reprieve in Europe from US trade data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar gets reprieve in Europe from US trade data.

text.p: The dollar recovered the bulk of overnight losses against the mark and firmed against the yen in Europe as a sharp drop in the March U.S. trade deficit helped offset some disappointment at the lack of a U.S. interest rate rise on Tuesday.
The U.S. trade gap shrank by 19.3 percent to $8.5 billion in March, well below market forecasts for a deficit in excess of $10 billion.
Moreover, a robust export performance is expected to prompt many economists to revise their first-quarter U.S. growth estimates to as high as six percent.
"The dollar will find some relief in the overall decline in the deficit," said Robert Hayward, economist at Bank of America.

However, analysts said dollar/mark was the most likely candidate to benefit longer-term and dollar/yen's bounce was The headline drop in the U.S. trade gap masked another 8.3 percent rise in the bilateral trade gap with Japan and is the sixth consecutive monthly rise there.
"This data shows the U.S. won't be particularly concerned with the recent turn of events in the currency markets," said Paul Meggyesi, currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The dollar/yen has collpased up to 14 percent this month

from its highest level in 4-1/2 years amid speculation about higher Japanese interest rates, official U.S. concern about the Japanese trade surplus and a barrage of Japanese offiical comments aimed at preventing further yen weakness.
At 1520 GMT, the dollar was trading at 114.25/30 yen compared with 113.65/75 late Tuesday and the 5-1/2-month low at 111.88 set yesterday.
Against the mark, it was at 1.6937/42 compared with 1.6960/70 late Tuesday.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin warned Japan earlier this week that it should not allow its trade surplus to balloon again. Commerce Department Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich reiterated that sentiment today and said Japan should not revert to its past pattern of export-led growth.

"We believe there is still a lot of position adjustment due in dollar/yen but interest rate expectations continue to help dollar/mark," said Meggyesi at Deutsche. "In this environment, we'll see the elastic in mark/yen continue to stretch."
Mark/yen steadied today after setting a 20-month low on Tuesday.
Traders said dollar/mark was undermined late Tuesday by disappointment at the lack of a rise in U.S. interest rates after the Federal Reserve's policy-making Open Market Committee.
However, analysts said another rise in U.S. rates is probably just a matter of time.

The dollar/mark gleaned verbal support from Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick who said he had little objection to the dollar at 1.70 marks. The dollar/Swiss franc also got support as the Swiss National Bank added liquidity to its local market to counter renewed Swiss franc strength.
